{{Recipe summary
| Category = Lamb recipes
}}

{{Recipe}}

== Ingredients ==

=== Lamb ===

* 1 leg of [[Cookbook:Lamb and Mutton|lamb]], sized according to the number of servings
* [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|Olive oil]]
* 8 cloves [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]]
* Fresh [[Cookbook:Rosemary|rosemary]] sprigs
* Fresh [[Cookbook:Thyme|thyme]] sprigs
* Fresh [[Cookbook:Lavender|lavender]] (optional)
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
* 400 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] cold water
* 400 ml white [[Cookbook:Wine|wine]]

=== Gravy ===

* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] dry red or white wine
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] mint sauce
* 1 tsp orange [[Cookbook:Marmalade|marmalade]]
* 1 tsp [[Cookbook:Mustard|mustard]]
* A generous grating of [[Cookbook:Nutmeg|nutmeg]]
* [[Cookbook:Worcestershire Sauce|Worcestershire]] or [[Cookbook:Liquid Seasoning|Maggi sauce]]

== Procedure ==

=== Lamb ===

# A full day before you intend to cook the lamb, rub it all over with a couple tablespoons of olive oil. Place the leg on a sheet of [[Cookbook:Aluminium Foil|aluminum foil]].
# Cut 8 small slits all over the skin of the leg. Insert a garlic clove into each slit.
# Rub the leg all over with a couple sprigs of each of rosemary, thyme, and lavender. Leave them on the joint, and wrap it in the aluminum foil.
# Place the leg in the fridge and let it rest overnight. Remember to turn the leg occasionally so the herbs infuse into all parts of the joint.
# Preheat the [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 180–200 °C.
# Cover the bottom of a roasting pan with as much rosemary, thyme, and lavender as will fit over the surface. Drizzle a couple tablespoons of olive oil over the top.
# Season the leg of lamb all over with salt, and place it on the bed of herbs.
# Pour the water and white wine over the leg. The purpose of this is to keep the meat moist as it roasts.
# [[Cookbook:Roasting|Roast]] the leg until it is medium-rare—about 20 minutes per pound (450 g), plus an extra 15 minutes. [[Cookbook:Basting|Baste]] every so often during the cooking.
# Transfer the leg to a serving dish, and tent it loosely with aluminum foil. Let rest in the kitchen for 15 minutes.

=== Gravy ===

# Remove the herb sprigs from the roasting pan, and transfer the pan to the stovetop over medium-high heat.
# When hot, add the wine, and [[Cookbook:Deglazing|deglaze]] everything.
# Add a dash of water, the mint sauce, marmalade, mustard, and nutmeg.
# [[Cookbook:Simmering|Simmer]] until the gravy reduces and thickens as desired—it will be a little like a ''jus''. Season with Worcestershire sauce to taste.
# [[Cookbook:Straining|Strain]] the gravy into a serving dish and serve with the lamb.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* If you are really feeling naughty, you can add some crème fraiche to the gravy!
* A few hand-torn mint-leaves, mixed with a little warm Greek honey and a good quality vinegar is a delightful addition to roast lamb.
